external_later_canonical_authority.statement: The LARE evidence remains bound to its frozen basis. F-ROMV2 canonical evidence is imported only to inform representation selection and comparator choice.

LARE.identity: Low-dimensional layer/storage representation with explicit conservative state and reconstructed hydraulic closure.
positive_evidence: State information location matters; compact lower-zone storage partitions can separate bounded groundwater states.
Terminal moving-control-volume accounting and B9 terminal-side qH closure are physically coherent.
The dominant remaining B9 internal-flux error is gradient-reconstruction rather than conductivity.
limiting_evidence: C4L qH-preserving cubic closure is mixed across width/regime.
C4N face-interpolated gradient helps FALL but fails RISE and HOLD.
C4O finds no single zero-fit existing-state conditioner transferable across both tested widths.
Further scalar blend/switch tuning is not authorized.

evidence.value: transparent benchmark for any more specialized reduced representation

TWO_LAYER_AND_QUASI_STEADY.diagnosis: Insufficient lower-zone/groundwater memory or lower-boundary flux closure.

FMC_SMVE.identity: Finite-water-content / Soil Moisture Velocity Equation physical reduction using moisture-content/front coordinates, explicit finite-volume water accounting and no global nonlinear Richards solve.
positive_evidence: D13 groundwater-front branch beats R2 on preregistered balance and transient groundwater-flux views.
D17 simultaneous separated surface+groundwater branch beats R2 on all preregistered views.
D19 exact contact/merge and early post-merge dynamics beat R2 on all preregistered views.
D20 one-hour relative advantage over R2 persists through the last quarter.
D22 native rainfall-threshold response is better-or-equal to R2 on all preregistered response views.
D23 short rainfall/redistribution trajectory beats R2 on every preregistered D23 frontier view.
unresolved_boundaries: Absolute bottom-flux error and systematic storage/bottom-exchange drift remain material in longer tests.
Upper-zone integrated storage can be worse than R2.
Native ponding/runoff thresholds are not equivalent to R16.
Live moving groundwater-table coupling in SWAP5 is not yet qualified.
ET/root uptake, drought/recovery, heterogeneous soils, seasonal/multi-year balance and application acceptance are not qualified.
No formal same-runtime production speedup is admitted.

scientific_reasoning: The LARE C4 chain no longer supports additional scalar closure invention: width/regime dependence survives multiple physically derived no-fit closure families.
Coarse Richards provides the mandatory transparent structural comparator but does not remove the nonlinear Richards solve and has weak lower-boundary event fidelity.
The two-layer/quasi-steady alternatives already tested in F-ROMV2 do not justify a new branch because they remain behind R2.

FMC/SMVE is the only reviewed distinct physical-reduction family with repeated bounded SWAP5 evidence crossing the R2 frontier on groundwater, combined surface-groundwater, merge and rainfall/redistribution views.
Therefore the next useful experiment is a matched-workload representation discriminator, not another LARE scalar closure.

next_experiment.title: Matched lower-boundary representation discriminator
next_experiment.objective: Compare LARE/B9, a retained coarse-Richards comparator and the literature-bound FMC/SMVE route on one shared bounded hydraulic workload chosen before exposure.
required_properties: same material and initial physical state
same forcing and lower-boundary semantics within all three representations' admitted authority
separate balance, state/profile, bottom-flux magnitude, sign/reversal and systematic-bias views
next_experiment.preferred_scope: A fixed-water-table or zero-head lower-boundary workload that lies inside existing FMC authority and can be represented by the current LARE boundary machinery without inventing new groundwater coupling.
